title: Pre-Analysis — Friction Damper Access Standard Against the Four-Engine Request
abstract: Closed work order confirming that the friction damper access standard was correctly limited to the twin-engine quadrant and identifying what a four-engine version would have to solve.

sections.objective: Confirm whether the friction damper access standard released for the twin-engine quadrant could be offered to four-engine operators, whose quadrant removal rate is three times the twin-engine figure and who have been asking for it since the standard was published.
sections.findings_summary: It cannot, and the reason is geometric rather than commercial. The four-engine quadrant carries four lever paths in the same pedestal envelope, and the top access latch that makes the friction pack serviceable on wing has nowhere to go. A side access is possible but is a different design and needs the cowl latch that the twin-engine standard deletes, so the two standards would diverge rather than converge. The single-channel resolver on a four-lever quadrant is a second issue that came up during the search and is arguably more valuable than the friction access: losing one channel takes a lever out of autothrust entirely rather than degrading it. The friction setting task already covers both routes, on wing where the latch is fitted and off wing where it is not, so no manual change is needed to say no to the operators.
sections.next_steps: Answer the four-engine operators with the geometric reason rather than a commercial one. Recommend that the resolver redundancy and the side access be scoped together as one four-engine candidate rather than separately. Take no action on the friction setting task.

evidence.similarity_note: Found by entity linking on the access latch and shroud part numbers the task calls out.

expected_findings.rationale: The friction setting task already covers both the on-wing and off-wing routes and selects between them on whether the access latch is fitted. Nothing has to change to keep the four-engine aircraft on the off-wing route.

evidence.similarity_note: Surfaced by similarity between the two subjects, which share the pedestal and the autothrust loop but no part number.

expected_findings.rationale: The four-engine autothrust gain set and any four-engine quadrant change touch the same lever angle signal from opposite ends. Scoping them separately would leave the interface between them undefined.
expected_findings.resolution: Scope the resolver redundancy and the side access as one candidate.

evidence.similarity_note: Found through the bulletin effectivity, which already excludes the four-engine aircraft.

expected_findings.rationale: The bulletin states the exclusion but not the reason, which is why operators keep asking. An effectivity note that explains itself would have prevented the question.
expected_findings.resolution: Add the geometric reason to the bulletin effectivity note at the next revision.

type_data.conclusion: Closed. The extension is not available; a four-engine candidate should carry both the access and the resolver work.
